title: The Oldest Customer Complaint on Record (Epic Frame style test)
sources: British Museum, museum no. 1953,0411.71 (BM 131236): clay tablet, letter from Nanni to Ea-nasir about the wrong grade of copper, from Ur, Old Babylonian period, c. 1750 BC (date approximate)
Guinness World Records, 'Oldest written customer complaint'

lines.text: Three thousand seven hundred years ago, a man in Ur paid for fine copper,
lines.caps: THREE *THOUSAND | SEVEN *HUNDRED YEARS AGO | A MAN IN *UR | PAID FOR *COPPER

lines.text: So he did what anyone would do.
He wrote the angriest letter he could.
It survives today in the British Museum,
the oldest customer complaint on record.
Some things never change, do they?
